title: 1959 AHSME Problem 27
statement:
Which one of the following statements is not true for the equation

\[ ix^2-x+2i=0, \]

where \(i=\sqrt{-1}?\)

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: The sum of the roots is \(2\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: The roots can be found by using the quadratic formula

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
The roots can be found by factoring, using imaginary
numbers

solutions.text:
By Vieta’s formula, the sum of the roots is \[ -\frac{-1}{i}=\frac1i=-i, \] not \(2.\) Also the discriminant is \[ (-1)^2-4(i)(2i)=1-8i^2=9. \] The quadratic formula gives the imaginary roots \(i\) and \(-2i,\) so the remaining statements are true.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Use Vieta’s formula for the sum of the roots before solving the equation
The sum is the negative of the \(x\)-coefficient divided by the \(x^2\)-coefficient
